role.altitude: The restoration planner keeps walking sites with landowners, surveying habitats, choosing measures, weighing options and building ecological models; looking up subsidy rules, writing standard measure texts, screening long literature lists, retyping field forms and preparing GIS layers by hand shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A planner who spends more time in the field and on choices, with data, texts and layers prepared from records.

tasks.short: Visit the land with the owner, develop recommendations to maintain or restore environmental conditions, check subsidy conditions, write the advice, approve and send it, and answer follow-up questions.

steps.what: Planner visits the land and talks with the landowner
Planner develops recommendations to maintain or restore environmental conditions on the land
Planner looks up subsidy schemes and conditions for the chosen measures
Planner writes the advice for the landowner with measures and maintenance
Planner checks and approves the final advice
Planner sends the advice to the landowner
Planner answers the landowner's follow-up questions

approvals.approved_version: The advice text with measures, maintenance and subsidy notes as approved by the planner in s5, addressed to the landowner who asked; any edit needs a new check before sending.

tasks.design: A measures catalogue holds, per restoration measure, a standard description, maintenance instructions and the subsidy schemes with their conditions. The planner picks measures and the catalogue fills those parts of the advice, instead of looking them up and rewriting them each time. The site visit, choosing the measures and the site-specific reasoning stay with the planner, who approves and sends the advice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measure texts and subsidy rules were looked up and rewritten for each landowner.
tasks.enabler_now: A measures catalogue with standard texts and subsidy conditions.
tasks.still_hard: Land with conflicting uses, such as farming and nature.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a measure the landowner will keep doing for years.
tasks.altitude: Less writing standard text; advising stays.

reach.learn: Whether advice arrives sooner and is followed.

evidence.claim: Catalogues of standard clauses fill recurring parts of advice documents.

assumptions: Boundary: advising landowners; habitat management plans (task 16875) and site assessments (task 16876) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3: subsidy conditions kept in the catalogue by the subsidy desk, for about 80% of measures; s3 is priced at that share.
Visiting, choosing, approving, sending and answering keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of landowner advices per year.
research_questions: Do more landowners apply for subsidies after advice?

incremental.description: Planner keeps the measures catalogue current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual land with few standard measures; high: many similar advices.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define remediation options, assemble site data, estimate costs, weigh benefits and risks, compare options, and write the feasibility and cost-benefit study for environmental remediation projects.

steps.what: Planner defines the remediation options to compare
Planner assembles site data and contamination results from earlier investigations
Planner estimates the costs of each remediation option
Planner weighs ecological benefits and risks of each option
Planner compares options on feasibility, cost and benefit and chooses the recommendation
Planner writes the feasibility and cost-benefit report

loop.input: The option tables, cost estimates and the planner's recommendation.
loop.output: A draft report in the study template.
loop.check: Every number must match the tables; any miss stops the draft; the planner rewrites the reasoning.
loop.stop: The planner writes the report by hand after two failed checks.

tasks.design: Earlier investigation results come from the project data store as tables per sample point, instead of being picked from old PDF reports. Cost estimates are quantities per option times a unit-price table of past remediation contracts. Defining options, weighing benefits and choosing stay with the planner. The report template fills tables, and a drafting step writes a first text from the planner's recommendation with every number checked against the tables.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data sat in old reports and costs were rebuilt in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Project data stores, unit-price tables and drafting checked against tables.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which cheap option will fail on this soil.

reach.learn: Whether studies are comparable across sites.

evidence.claim: Cost estimates are quantities times a unit-price table; drafting is checked against the tables.

assumptions: Boundary: feasibility and cost-benefit studies; collecting and analysing condition data (task 16872) and project budgets (task 16856) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: investigation results loaded into the project data store through task 16872, for about 70% of sites; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3: unit-price table kept from past contracts, covering about 70% of cost items; s3 is priced at that share.
Defining, weighing and choosing keep their full time.
research_questions: Do estimates match final project costs more closely?

incremental.description: Planner keeps the unit-price table current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new techniques and old paper data; high: repeat options with data in the store.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scope the study, review literature and earlier studies, survey species and habitats, record field observations, analyse ecological effects of pollutants, disease, human activities and climate change, and write the impact study.

steps.what: Planner scopes the environmental impact study
Planner reviews literature and earlier studies on the ecological effects

loop.input: Titles and abstracts from the literature search.
loop.output: The results reordered so the likely relevant come first, while the planner labels each one read.
loop.check: The stop rule, fixed beforehand, is tested on known relevant studies.
loop.stop: Screening stops when the fixed rule is met; below it the planner screens on.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevance depends on the species and site.

steps.what: Planner surveys species and habitats in the field
Planner records field observations on paper forms and types them up
Planner analyses the ecological effects of pollutants, disease, human activities and climate change
Planner writes the impact study report

loop.input: The planner's assessment, observation tables and the reference list of screened studies.
loop.output: A draft report in the study template.
loop.check: Every number must match a table and every reference must be in the screened list; any miss stops the draft.
loop.stop: The planner writes the section by hand after two failed checks.

tasks.design: An active learning screener reorders literature search results while the planner labels them, with a stop rule fixed and tested beforehand. Field observations go into a field app with species lists and location, instead of paper forms typed up later. Scoping, surveying and analysing stay with the planner. The report template fills tables, and a drafting step writes a first text with every number and reference checked against the tables and the screened list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature was screened one by one and field forms typed up.
tasks.still_hard: Effects that need several seasons of observation.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a disease effect from a drought effect in the field.
tasks.altitude: Less sifting and typing; fieldwork and analysis stay.

reach.learn: Whether studies cite more of the relevant evidence.

evidence.claim: On one published review of 5,808 references, active learning found all 28 included studies after screening 746, in 92 minutes against 1,018.
An open-source screener reorders abstracts while a person screens.
In 84 generated literature reviews, 18% to 55% of references were fabricated, so references come only from the screened list.

assumptions: Boundary: impact studies; identifying impacts of remediation activities (task 16866) and communicating findings (task 16871) are sibling tasks.
Impact studies screen hundreds of studies, so s2 is priced well below the published benchmark.
s4 saves the second entry of paper field forms.
Scoping, surveying and analysing keep their full time.
research_questions: Does assisted screening miss any study a full screen finds?

already_counted.description: Planner rewrites the drafted report sections.

incremental.description: Planner tests the stop rule and keeps field app species lists current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: field-heavy studies with little literature; high: broad literature reviews and many observations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define the model and its ecological assumptions, prepare GIS inputs, build the environmental model or simulation, run scenarios, calibrate against field data, and document it.

steps.what: Planner defines the model's purpose and ecological assumptions from knowledge of the ecosystems
Planner gathers and prepares geographic information system data: land cover, elevation, water and species records
Planner builds and parameterises the environmental model
Planner runs the simulations for each scenario
Planner calibrates the model against field observations
Planner documents the model, data and assumptions

tasks.design: Rerunnable scripts fetch and clip land cover, elevation and water data for the study area from open data services, instead of the planner downloading and processing each layer by hand. Scenario runs are scripted in a batch. Defining the model, building it and calibrating it against field data stay with the planner. Data sources and parameters are written into the model documentation from the script's settings file.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layers were downloaded and processed by hand for each model.
tasks.enabler_now: Rerunnable scripts over open satellite data.
tasks.still_hard: Species data that are sparse or unpublished.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which ecological process the model must capture.

reach.learn: Whether models are rerun when data change.

evidence.claim: A European data service runs rerunnable scripts over satellite datacubes for land cover maps.

assumptions: Boundary: environmental models; GIS diagrams for planning (task 16858) and planning projects with biological databases (task 16865) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: open data cover land cover, elevation and water for the study area; species records still need requests.
Defining, building and calibrating keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of models built per year.
research_questions: Are models rerun more often when data change?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off models with special data; high: repeat models over open data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
